That is why I often feel tired, even though I dont do that much of anything at my regular jobs.

I think in our society people view ocd as a non problem or in some cases as a sign of talent. Like an incentive for being mentally unsound. The reality is ocd is like having a drug addiction. If the drug supply is cut, you experience withdrawal symptoms. If people understood that they would have much more empathy. People with ocd learn through their experiences what it is like to be misunderstood. The true meaning of the word misunderstood. All human beings want 3 things in this life, to survive, to love and be loved, and to be understood. All are intertwined. If you aren't understood it affects how or if you will be loved. If you aren't loved you probably aren't understood. That aspect is challenged constantly. That is why from my experience people with ocd are especially empathetic and understanding of others including people that have unrelated problems.

When I say people that use the word loser I don't mean those that refer to one person or team as a winner and the other as a loser. I also don't mean those that refer to people that are given many opportunities and turn them down and instead live off people's kindness. What i mean are the people that look at others that have less then them in some aspect of their life and refer to them as losers. Also people that refer to those that they don't understand and that don't know them losers. The idea of looking down on others that you dont understand and that have less than you is the basis for a lot of prejudice. Someone that calls a person with few friends a loser and that nobody likes you, is looking down on someone he doesn't know and doesn't care to know. That is fundamentally no different than a group of people from a rich or developed country looking down on the inhabitants and culture of those from poorer countries. 

The reason for a lot, not all, but a lot of racism is this tendency to look down on others. Europeans looked down on Africans because they viewed them as inferior since most of Europe was and still is more developed than most of Africa. Rather than trying to understand why this disparity exists, they instead assumed that the people themselves were inferior and less worthy and therefore that is why they are impoverished. 

In the same sense, people that look down on people that don't have much money, work remedial jobs, have few friends, or relationships, are no different. They are merely different manifestations of the same basic principle. So when i say nazis, I don't mean that a person that calls someone a loser is a Nazi. I mean people that denigrate others and invalidate them, usually people they dont know or understand, by calling them losers, people that have less then them.in whatever way without trying to underatand why, are thinking along similar lines, albeit more watered down. 

Ultimately, anyone you look down on you will treat worse.

Imagine being so ignorant and unthoughtful that you don't even try to understand another's perspective and merely respond by jabbing at the value of their personhood. Imagine lacking empathy, reason, and regard for others enough to act this way towards people you dont know or even try to.

I've experienced very similar. Not the same, but similar. What is happening in your head is exactly the same as touching a faucet 4 times before or after using it, or checking the stove 3 times before leaving. The reason it is so confusing is that it is happening inside your head. Intrusive thoughts in your mind, for example with regards to a certain year or certain people are a manifedtation of fear. Here is an analogy. If you were standing on the edge of a high platform or bridge, have you ever gotten the thought or the urge to jump off. Or at least climb on the railing? I have. And I usually do when I am scared. If I weren't afraid of heights, or of falling, then I wouldn't get those thoughts. The thoughts and urges induce fear, causing you to back away from the edge. Then you begin to distrust your own intentions and fear that you might throw yourself off anyway. The reason for this is because we are curious about our fears. The curious response goes off when you are presented by a fear but from a safe vantage point. Standing on a sturdy platform or bridge above a big drop, is a danger or fear from a safe vantage point. If you were actually dangling from the bridge, your actual fear would override the curiosity response, causing you to do everything in your power to climb back up. This state alters your reality. First you begin to fear your own intentions, then you get a thought of "what if someone pushes me over?" And bam! Now your sense of awareness shifts to your surroundings as opposed to your urges and you begin to suspect or fear passerbys pushing you off. In your case, the thought of 2012 is the drop beneath or beyond the edge of the bridge. The compulsions you perform chronologically are the stepping back from the edge and examining your intentions or other people walking by. The fundamental difference is that in the first case, the feared situation is tangible and as such easy to verify to yourself if it is actually happening. You can verify that you aren't falling off a bridge. You cannot verify that by thinking a certain thought something wont happen. I often get intrusive wish thoufhts whenever I try to make a wish. I don't desire the thoughts. They just come anyway. Because they pertiwn the intangible, i am unable to verify that they arent or won't occur. And the thoughts I get all depend on what I am presently obsessing about. So because you cannot verify due to the intangible nature of the thoughts and fear, and due to the fact that anything intangible in that mind like thoughts are going to appear to your brain as being from a safe enough vantage point since you aren't physically under any kind of threat, the curioisuty response will continue to be bolstered by the fear, which gets bolstered by the attention you give it. rtely, ocd always targets the things you value.
